description: Put your mouse and keyboard on the dyno: polling rate, clicks, keys, sensor, real DPI and reaction time. Everything runs in this window; nothing is recorded.

polling.hint: Move the mouse quickly in circles inside the pad: KeyHalo measures how often it reports.
polling.prompt: Move your mouse here in fast circles
polling.overTimeSub: One sample every 250 ms while moving
polling.histogramSub: Share of reports by nearest polling rate (Hz)
polling.noData: Move the mouse in the pad to start
polling.note: Browsers can only see what the OS delivers: slow movement, power saving or a busy system lower the reading. Rates above 1000 Hz need a fast, smooth motion.

clicks.hint: Click inside the pad as fast as you can. Two presses of the same button closer than {ms} ms are flagged as a possible double-click fault.
clicks.prompt: Click here to start the {s}-second test
clicks.result: {clicks} clicks in {s} s · click to try again
clicks.logSub: Interval since the previous press of the same button · flagged under {ms} ms
clicks.noClicks: Press any mouse button in the pad, side buttons included

keys.hint: Press every key: tested keys stay tinted, held keys light up, and a re-press within {ms} ms of a release is flagged as chatter.
keys.rolloverHint: Hold many keys at once (N-key rollover)
keys.noKeys: Press a key to see its codes
keys.noteFn: Fn never reaches the computer: the keyboard handles it internally, so it can't be tested here.
keys.noteOs: Windows keeps some shortcuts for itself (Win key combos, Alt+Tab, Ctrl+Alt+Del) and Print Screen only reports its release.
keys.noteNkro: If a key doesn't register while others are held, you've hit the keyboard's rollover limit (ghosting/blocking).

sensor.hint: Lock the pointer, then hold the left button and draw straight horizontal lines: raw counts reveal jitter, smoothing and angle snapping.
sensor.prompt: Raw movement is drawn here; the cursor is hidden while locked
sensor.snapping: Your lines are almost perfectly level and straight: the sensor is probably applying angle snapping (straightening). Check the mouse software or firmware.
sensor.snappingHint: Tip: draw slow, slightly diagonal lines. If they come out perfectly horizontal or stair-stepped, the sensor has angle snapping.

dpi.hint: Measure the real DPI: move the mouse an exact distance along a ruler and compare the counts with the DPI you set.
dpi.step1: Put a ruler on the desk and line the mouse up with its 0 mark.
dpi.step2: Lock the pointer, hold the left button and move exactly {d} in a straight line.
dpi.step3: Release. Repeat a few times; the average is your real DPI.
dpi.holdToMeasure: Hold the left button and move
dpi.noMouse: No mouse connected: enter its DPI
dpi.note: A deviation within ±3 % is normal. The bar under the ruler shows how far the configured DPI says you've moved.
dpi.adjustedWarning: Raw input isn't available here: Windows pointer speed and "Enhance pointer precision" can skew the counts. Set speed to 10 and turn acceleration off for this test.

reaction.hint: Click (or press Space) as soon as the pad turns green. {n} tries; clicking early doesn't count.
reaction.earlySub: That one doesn't count · click to retry
reaction.doneSub: Average of 5 · click to start over
reaction.note: Most people land between 200 and 300 ms. Results include your monitor and mouse latency, which this test can't separate.
